title: CDC and NIH Biomedical Research Destruction - $18 Billion Federal Science Elimination
description_short: CDC and NIH Biomedical Research Destruction - $18 Billion Federal Science Elimination
description_medium: Nature reported that NIH had terminated nearly 800 research projects by April 2025. A separate Science report described a proposed FY2026 NIH budget of $26.7 billion and a reorganization that would require congressional approval. Those reports do not establish an enacted $18 billion cut, a final NIH appropriation or the specific effects of changes to CDC programs.
description_long: The linked reporting describes disruption to federal biomedical research, but not a completed $18 billion reduction across NIH and CDC. Nature reported that NIH had terminated nearly 800 research projects by April 2025. STAT described instability among researchers whose grants were disrupted. Science separately reported an administration proposal to reduce the NIH budget to $26.7 billion in fiscal year 2026 and reorganize the agency; that proposal required congressional approval. A proposed budget is not an enacted appropriation, and the project count does not establish a final dollar reduction or show that every affected award ended permanently. The supplied sources also do not identify which CDC chronic-disease programs ended, when changes took effect or what services were affected. These reports document project terminations, funding instability and a proposed NIH budget change. They do not establish an enacted $18 billion cut or show that CDC programs ended. Enacted appropriations, project-level cancellation records and CDC program notices are needed to state the final amounts and effects.
subcategory: Biomedical Research Elimination and Federal Science Destruction
organization_tags: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Donald Trump Jr. is paid $50,000 to meet with Russian assets in Paris
description_short: Donald Trump Jr. is paid $50,000 to meet with Russian assets in Paris
description_medium: The linked account says Donald Trump Jr. attended a private gathering at the Ritz in Paris in October 2016 and received at least $50,000. It identifies the organizer as the Center for Political and Foreign Affairs and describes the group as tied to Russian influence. The page does not provide payment records or the underlying French intelligence assessment supporting its characterization of attendees as Russian assets.
description_long: According to the linked account, Donald Trump Jr. attended a private event of about 30 people at the Ritz Hotel in Paris in October 2016 and received at least $50,000. The gathering was hosted by the Center for Political and Foreign Affairs. The account describes organizers Fabien Baussart and Randa Kassis as having ties to Russian officials; Kassis said she later discussed the meeting with Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov and hoped a Trump victory would enable cooperation with the United States over Syria. She also said she conveyed an idea through Trump Jr. These statements are attributed to the organizer and do not establish that Trump Jr. delivered a policy proposal to his father or that any agreement resulted. The linked page calls the event’s participants Russian intelligence assets and attributes that assessment to French intelligence, but does not include the underlying assessment or payment documentation. A contemporaneous contract, payment record and intelligence assessment would be needed to verify the amount and characterization. The available account documents a reported paid appearance and attributed follow-up contacts, but does not independently verify an intelligence meeting.
topic_tags: Center for Political and Foreign Affairs
organization_tags: Center for Political and Foreign Affairs

title: Trump: State Dept. blocks autopsy results of Trump-Russia figure Vitaly Churkin
description_short: Trump: State Dept. blocks autopsy results of Trump-Russia figure Vitaly Churkin
description_medium: Vitaly Churkin, Russia’s U.N. ambassador, died in New York on February 20, 2017. The city medical examiner initially said toxicology was needed before determining the cause and later did not release the autopsy results. The linked account alleges federal pressure and Russian objections, but supplies no records documenting who requested withholding or under what authority. It also does not show Trump influenced the decision.
description_long: Vitaly Churkin, Russia’s ambassador to the United Nations, died in New York on February 20, 2017. The linked timeline says the city medical examiner’s office initially could not determine the cause without toxicology and later declined to release the autopsy results. It alleges that federal officials lobbied New York City to withhold the findings and direct inquiries to the State Department, citing a claimed legal obligation and Russia’s objection to disclosure. The account does not include letters or other independent records documenting the lobbying, so the extent and authority of any federal request remain unverified. It also says Churkin met Donald Trump at a 1986 luncheon and later defended him at the United Nations. Those earlier contacts do not establish that Trump influenced the medical examiner’s decision. The available reporting describes a non-release and an alleged federal role, but does not give the controlling legal rule or establish who made the decision. The pressure claim should remain attributed until official correspondence or other records are available.
organization_tags: New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner

title: Trump: Epstein consults Ken Starr to protect Trump
description_short: Trump: Epstein consults Ken Starr to protect Trump
description_medium: Trump File reports that Jeffrey Epstein emailed on August 23, 2018, saying he had spoken with attorney Ken Starr the previous day, when Michael Cohen pleaded guilty to campaign-finance violations connected to Trump. Starr later joined Trump’s Senate impeachment defense. The linked page does not include the full email exchange or show that advice reached Trump.
description_long: Michael Cohen pleaded guilty on August 22, 2018, to campaign-finance violations connected to payments for the Trump campaign. Trump File reports that Epstein emailed the next day saying he had spoken with attorney Ken Starr the previous day. Starr later joined Trump’s Senate impeachment defense in 2020. The chronology places Epstein’s reported conversation with Starr on the day of Cohen’s plea, but the linked page does not reproduce the full email thread or establish what the two discussed. It does not identify all senders and recipients, show that Trump was part of the exchange, or demonstrate that Starr gave him advice through Epstein. Nor does it connect the conversation to a change in the legal outcome. The report supports a narrow account of an email describing a conversation between Epstein and Starr, followed later by Starr’s role in Trump’s impeachment defense. The claim that Epstein consulted Starr to protect Trump goes beyond the available summary; the discussion’s subject and any effect on Trump remain unverified.

title: Trump tells China's president he approves of Muslim concentration camps
description_short: Trump tells China's president he approves of Muslim concentration camps
description_medium: Former national security adviser John Bolton later wrote that Donald Trump expressed approval of China’s detention camps for Muslim minorities during a private conversation with Xi Jinping at the June 2019 G20 summit. The linked account also cites Matthew Pottinger’s recollection of a similar exchange in 2017. Neither source is a transcript, and the packet does not establish the exact wording or full context of the 2019 conversation.
description_long: The linked account attributes to former national security adviser John Bolton a private conversation between Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the opening dinner of the June 2019 G20 summit in Osaka. Bolton later wrote that Trump expressed approval of China’s detention camps for Muslim minorities while Xi explained the policy. The account also cites Matthew Pottinger’s recollection of a similar exchange in 2017. These are retrospective descriptions of private remarks, not a public transcript or official finding. The materials do not establish the exact wording, whether Trump used the phrase “concentration camps,” or the full context of the discussion. They also do not show what policy decisions followed from the reported remarks. If accurately recalled, the exchange concerned a U.S. president’s response to China’s detention policy in Xinjiang. The recollections support an attributed account, not a transcript-confirmed quotation or independently verified statement.

preserved_fields.title: Trump tells China's president he approves of Muslim concentration camps
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump tells China's president he approves of Muslim concentration camps

notes: Needs context: the account relies on retrospective recollections and provides no transcript or contemporaneous record establishing exact wording and context. Proposed correction: attribute the claim to Bolton and Pottinger rather than state the quoted characterization as independently verified.
